original_value: Falls are the major cause of fatal and non-fatal injury among people aged more than 65 years. Due to the grave consequences of the occurrence of falls, it is necessary to conduct thorough research on falls. This paper presents a method for the study of fall detection using surface electromyography (sEMG) based on an improved dual parallel channels convolutional neural network (IDPC-CNN). The proposed IDPC-CNN model is designed to identify falls from daily activities using the spectral features of sEMG. Firstly, the classification accuracy of time domain features and spectrograms are compared using linear discriminant analysis (LDA), k-nearest neighbor (KNN) and support vector machine (SVM). Results show that spectrograms provide a richer way to extract pattern information and better classification performance. Therefore, the spectrogram features of sEMG are selected as the input of IDPC-CNN to distinguish between daily activities and falls. Finally, The IDPC-CNN is compared with SVM and three different structure CNNs under the same conditions. Experimental results show that the proposed IDPC-CNN achieves 92.55% accuracy, 95.71% sensitivity and 91.7% specificity. Overall, The IDPC-CNN is more effective than the comparison in accuracy, efficiency, training and generalization.

result.paraphrase: Falls are a leading cause of both fatal and non-fatal injuries in people over 65 years old. Because the consequences of falls are severe, detailed research on them is necessary. This paper proposes a fall-detection study method based on surface electromyography (sEMG) and an improved dual parallel channels convolutional neural network (IDPC-CNN). The model is intended to distinguish falls from daily activities by using spectral features of sEMG. First, classification performance for time-domain features and spectrograms is compared with linear discriminant analysis (LDA), k-nearest neighbor (KNN), and support vector machine (SVM). The results indicate that spectrograms offer richer pattern information extraction and better classification performance. Accordingly, spectrogram features of sEMG are used as the input to IDPC-CNN for separating daily activities from falls. Finally, IDPC-CNN is evaluated against SVM and three CNNs with different structures under the same conditions. The experiments show that the proposed IDPC-CNN reaches 92.55% accuracy, 95.71% sensitivity, and 91.7% specificity. Overall, IDPC-CNN outperforms the comparisons in accuracy, efficiency, training, and generalization.
